jamie lopez: Hi team — my partner's child (stepchild) will be moving in next month and we want to add them to medical + dental. They're currently on a guardian arrangement overseas. Quick questions: 1) what documentation do you need for a stepchild added due to change in household/guardianship, esp for international docs? 2) can we make coverage effective the move-in date or does it have to be the guardianship court date? 3) will adding a dependent change my life insurance beneficiary rules? 4) can I add Dependent Care FSA midyear to cover childcare once they're here? Also worried about payroll proration/retro and spreading any retro premium out. Thanks!

nina (People Ops): Congrats on the family change, @jamie. Short answers up top: 1) For stepchildren we accept a notarized guardianship/custody order OR a signed guardian declaration plus proof of child identity (passport/birth cert). For international docs we need either an apostille OR a certified English translation. Please upload via the dependent add portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/dependent-add and choose "Change in Household / Guardianship". 2) Effective date: carriers usually allow the coverage effective date to be the date the child becomes part of your household if you enroll within the 30-day QLE window. If you have a court/guardian order with a different date, we can align to that; note carriers will confirm and may require the order date.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: QLE window is 30 days from event. Upload evidence to the portal to avoid delays: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle-policy :information_source:

alex (Benefits): Adding carrier notes: life insurance beneficiary designation is separate from dependent enrollment. Adding a dependent does NOT automatically change your beneficiary forms. If you want your new stepchild named as a beneficiary for basic or supplemental life, submit a beneficiary update via HR forms: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/beneficiary-update. Also check any state-specific minor trust language if you're naming a minor.

jamie lopez: Good to know re beneficiary. For Dependent Care FSA — can I add it now as a QLE?

nina (People Ops): Yes, a change in household — adding a stepchild — qualifies as a QLE for Dependent Care FSA election changes. Update your election in the portal and choose the QLE date as the child's move-in date. Note that dependent care FSA requires eligible expenses to be for qualifying dependents under IRS rules.

alex (Benefits): Carrier processing note: international guardianship docs sometimes trigger extra review (7-21 business days). Enroll immediately in our system with your requested effective date so carrier processing begins. Dental enrollments are separate but use the same dependent workflow.

jamie lopez: About payroll — if I pick effective date two weeks before the next paycheck will payroll do a retro catchup? Could I ask to spread the retro over two paychecks?

payroll-bot: Payroll response: premiums are prorated from the coverage effective date. If that date precedes the last payroll run, a retro premium adjustment will be applied on the next paycheck. We can request to split the retro amount across two consecutive pay runs — add that note in the portal request or reply here and we'll flag the case to payroll ops.

nina (People Ops): Practical file naming recommendation: lopez_jamie_stepchild_guardian.pdf and lopez_stepchild_passport.pdf; include translator's statement if using a certified translation. If you'd like us to upload on your behalf, DM the files and we can submit.

jamie lopez: Uploaded guardian order (translated) + passport to the portal and left a note to split retro over two paychecks. Thanks for the quick help! :raised_hands:

people-ops-bot: Received docs. Case opened and assigned to benefits ops. We'll update this thread once carriers/payload confirm processing times. :information_source:
